title: Precision-profile CI gatekeeper and regression watchdog for quant artifacts
creator: Aisha Reddy
description: Add a robust CI/validation and staged-publish workflow for quantization profile artifacts (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ). The goal is to prevent performance regressions and functional failures when shipping quant profiles to model-serving. This ticket builds a gatekeeper check in our quant profile CI, plus a lightweight 'watchdog' that runs post-publish canaries and triggers automatic mitigation/rollback hooks when key signals degrade.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI gate rejects quant profile artifacts that regress latency or accuracy beyond configurable thresholds across a standardized prompt set.
2) Artifacts that pass CI are published to a 'canary' channel and automatically enrolled into a telemetry watch for 48h.
3) Automated rollback or fallback policy triggers if canary signals exceed thresholds (latency spike, token-error rate, quality loss).
4) Dashboard shows per-artifact baseline, canary deviation, and regression root-cause link.
5) Documentation and runbook exist for operators to run manual re-eval and approve an override.
proposed_solution:
1) Extend the existing quant CI harness to run both microbenchmarks (latency p50/p95, mem) and a quality eval (standard prompt set + automated LLM-based pass/fail heuristics) across supported runners (hosted runtime, dedicated).
2) Introduce a 'Precision Profile Gate' step that compares results vs. pinned baseline artifacts stored in artifact registry. Thresholds should be per-model and per-precision (configurable YAML).
3) On publish, profiles go to 'canary' namespace and trigger a short-lived canary rollout to a small percentage of traffic or synthetic traffic runner. Telemetry collectors (token latency, error rates, quality delta, perplexity) will feed a Watchdog service.
4) Watchdog implements simple policy rules: alert on >10% median latency increase or >2% quality drop vs baseline, escalate to incident if >20%/5% respectively; optionally auto-fallback to higher-precision variant or previous profile.
5) Expose flags in Console for manual approvals and forced promotions.
6) Provide an opt-in debug mode that collects per-token traces and kernel selection logs for failed canaries.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (week 1-2): Implement CI gate tests and baseline comparison for a small set of models (Llama-2-7B, Redwood-compat open model).
Phase 2 (week 3): Publish canary channel and integrate Watchdog telemetry hooks; run synthetic canaries.
Phase 3 (week 4): Pilot with two internal customers and Dedicated env; iterate thresholds.
Phase 4 (week 5): Console UX for approvals and metrics; documentation and runbook.
Full rollout after two successful pilot cycles and stakeholder signoff.
monitoring_metrics:
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms)
- Token drop/error rate (exceptions, invalid tokens)
- Quality score delta (deterministic prompt set + eval heuristics)
- Model output divergence (embedding distance vs baseline)
- Memory pressure / OOM events
- Canary pass rate and time-to-detect (minutes)
test_plan:
- Unit tests for CI harness comparing measurements to stored baselines.
- Integration test: simulate a failing quant profile (known bad GPTQ seed) and assert CI gate rejects.
- End-to-end test: publish to canary channel, run synthetic traffic, assert Watchdog detects regression and auto-fallback triggers.
- Load test: run the CI microbench pipeline under parallel profile validation to ensure it completes within time budget.
- Manual QA: run developer-provided prompt suites and inspect per-token traces for 3 profiles.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: False positives from noisy quality heuristics. Mitigation: require multi-metric agreement (quality + latency) and add a short quarantine window before auto-rollback.
Risk: CI runtime cost increase. Mitigation: incremental sampling, reuse cached KV/prefix data, tiered checks (fast smoke vs full regression).
Risk: Canary telemetry gaps in Dedicated/private installs. Mitigation: provide a light-weight local collector and offline upload path.
